notes: Conceptual questions. Every case forbids every weather tool: a definition needs no forecast, and retrieving one would produce numbers nobody asked about. Each names the corpus documents that are actually relevant, so retrieval quality is scored against a declared expectation rather than against whatever came back.

cases.description: A concept people routinely misread, so the corpus document exists to correct it.
cases.question: What does a 40% chance of rain actually mean?

cases.description: A distinction between two measures, which the answer must keep apart.
cases.question: Explain the difference between wind gusts and sustained wind speed

cases.description: An index rather than a measurement, so the answer must explain the scale.
cases.question: What does the UV index measure?

cases.description: Why confidence falls with horizon distance — the concept behind every uncertainty statement.
cases.question: Why does forecast confidence decrease further into the future?

cases.description: A concept whose relationship to another measure the corpus explains.
cases.question: What is relative humidity?

cases.description: A concept the corpus does not cover: said plainly rather than answered from the nearest passage.
cases.question: Explain the quarterly corporation tax filing deadline
